analysis.title: UBS STIR Weekly: Wake Me Up Before You Hike-Hike
key_insights: Last week saw a broader risk-off move across global rates, but local central-bank dynamics drove divergence across regions.
USD rates rallied sharply midweek, with the back whites rallying over 20bp, on weakness in AI-related equities and despite higher oil. Payer interest in the October meeting was little.

USD pricing still embeds just under one hike through year-end and roughly 40bp of hikes into the middle of next year. Flow was subdued, with marginally better SOFR paying in the front end and interest in paying next year's turn.

EUR markets were dominated by wider German-French spreads, broader credit spread pressure, falling EUR basis and fading front-end funding support. After Friday's close Moody's left France unchanged, and since then basis has recovered and funding has been strong again.

ECB expectations softened. No hike is expected at the October meeting. December pricing fell to roughly 18-19bp, firmed to 21bp on Monday, then was offered after an MNI article citing a Eurosystem source saying a December hike is less certain because higher bond yields substitute for some tightening.

CHF outright has traded with a beta to EUR. The December SNB meeting prices around 3bp of hikes, and with 3m real-money rolls starting in November and a low probability of a hike, receiving December looks attractive.

The market prices roughly one full SNB hike by June 2027, with around 13bp priced for March and 17.5bp for June. The desk likes receiving late whites and reds on CHF basis versus EUR on a toppish cross-market level and on carry.

Japan nationwide CPI rose 2.1% y/y in September from 1.7% in August. BoJ research data show a persistently strong inflation trend since July across ex-fresh food, ex-food and energy, and trimmed mean measures, in both goods and services.
An October BoJ hold is the widely held base case, with almost no chance of a hike priced into Friday after BoJ messaging via media outlets. Front-end OIS up to 6m is better bid.
JPY funding is very strong at -5 FX/OIS, and -14 FX/OIS in 1m despite month-end flows. The very front-end paid remains attractive. JPY XCCY moves higher alongside risk-on sentiment in G10 XCCY.

Australia was an exception to the risk-off theme. RBA Deputy Governor Hauser said the inflation forecast would need to be revised higher at the November meeting, which prompted a hawkish repricing, with around 16bp priced for the meeting. UBS continues to expect a November hike. The move is concentrated in the front meeting and the rest of the curve is stable.

risk_factors: French political and funding concerns can widen German-French spreads and pressure EUR basis.
Weakness in AI-related equities drove the USD rates rally and could continue to move front-end pricing.
ECB December hike pricing is sensitive to headlines, as the MNI report showed.
A hawkish BoJ surprise is a risk to JPY rates, given the strong inflation trend, although almost no hike is priced for October.
vol_and_positioning: USD payer interest was limited in the October meeting despite the rally. Front-end SOFR paying was marginally better and there was interest in paying next year's turn.
EUR basis positioning appears somewhat cleaner than several weeks earlier. EUR basis ground lower during the week and has recovered since Friday's Moody's decision.
Receiving late whites and reds on CHF basis versus EUR is attractive at a toppish cross-market level on a time-series basis and on carry.
AUD hawkish repricing came with a decent amount of paying, concentrated in the front meeting.
geopolitical: Moody's decided not to downgrade France, which eased EUR basis and funding pressure after a week of German-French spread widening and French political concerns.
